EM-ORG-01.name: Company and Company Group
EM-ORG-01.scope: Business identity of an organization and an explicitly justified group perimeter. Legal personality and ownership shares belong to neighboring models.
specific_questions: When are the business and the legal entity a single object?
Which independent group perimeters are needed by management, consolidation and the market?
How is identity preserved through rebranding, sale and business split?
proposed_invariants: Basis and inclusion date are mandatory
A brand does not prove control
A group perimeter does not assign an owner to all facts of its members
EM-ORG-01.negative_case: Three companies with the same brand are automatically merged into one legal entity.
EM-ORG-01.acceptance_scenario: On a synthetic franchise and holding example, show distinct graphs of brand, management and control; rebranding does not create a new identity.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-02.name: Legal Identity and Registration
EM-ORG-02.scope: The legal subject, registry records, branches and legal succession. A registry record has its own identity and a verifiable basis.
specific_questions: Which attributes distinguish an independent entity from a branch?
How are LEI, tax and registration numbers linked without false identity?
Which changes continue an identity, and which create a legal successor?
proposed_invariants: A number is unique within its scheme and jurisdiction
Registration status does not substitute for the subject's status
Succession does not overwrite the parties of old contracts
EM-ORG-02.negative_case: A new extract from a different registry creates a second company.
EM-ORG-02.acceptance_scenario: One subject with three registrations, a branch without separate legal personality, and a merger must give correct answers as of a historical date.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-03.name: Ownership, Control and Corporate Governance
EM-ORG-03.scope: Participation, votes, control, governing bodies, mandates and decisions. Investment value and financial postings remain in the financial models.
specific_questions: How are equity, voting rights, contractual control and consolidation distinguished?
How are indirect relationships computed under cross-ownership?
Which powers and quorum confirm a specific decision?
proposed_invariants: Shares are comparable only within one class and period
Participation does not equal sole control
A decision references an active mandate and procedure
EM-ORG-03.negative_case: A 51% economic share automatically means 51% of votes and the authority to sign any contract.
EM-ORG-03.acceptance_scenario: Verify two share classes, cross-ownership, a change in board composition, and a decision without quorum.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-04.name: Organizational Unit and Mandate
EM-ORG-04.scope: A unit as a stable unit of responsibility. The org chart is a separate landscape; a team may be an independent collective.
specific_questions: What makes a unit an independent object?
How are administrative, functional and legal affiliation kept apart?
How are OUMM and the current WM-ORG-002 reconciled without two owners of unit?
proposed_invariants: A parent is scoped by axis, scenario and period
Renaming preserves the ID
Managerial affiliation does not determine the employer
EM-ORG-04.negative_case: A product team drawn from different departments is forced under a single administrative parent.
EM-ORG-04.acceptance_scenario: An as-is/to-be restructuring preserves old assignments and does not produce a cycle in the chosen administrative axis.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-05.name: Collectives, Teams and Membership
EM-ORG-05.scope: Teams, temporary collectives and communities of practice; time-bounded membership and working agreements. Membership must not be conflated with employment or authority.
specific_questions: Which collectives have their own purpose and lifecycle?
When is TechnicalDomain a classifier, and when a managed practice?
How are Collective and WM-ORG-003/006 combined without copying members?
proposed_invariants: Membership has a period and a basis
A member may belong to several collectives
Rights and funding are not derived from the member list
EM-ORG-05.negative_case: A community-of-practice member gets access to all products of its members.
EM-ORG-05.acceptance_scenario: Assemble a temporary cross-company team and a permanent community; verify the independence of membership, employment relationships and access.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-06.name: Positions, Roles and Responsibility
EM-ORG-06.scope: Staff positions and functional roles; responsibility, decision rights and RACI. The assignment of a person is held by the work relationship, and grade definitions are kept separately.
specific_questions: What exists independently of a person: a position, a role or a profession?
How are job sharing and roles without a staff position supported?
Where does responsibility end and technical IAM authority begin?
proposed_invariants: A vacant position is allowed
A business role is not an access role
RACI specifies the subject, role, period and permitted conflicts
EM-ORG-06.negative_case: Deleting an employee deletes the staff position and its budget.
EM-ORG-06.acceptance_scenario: Changing the incumbent preserves the position; one person performs two roles; two partial engagements may occupy one position under a permitted profile.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-ORG-07.name: Stakeholder and Engagement
EM-ORG-07.scope: The contextual relationship of a person or organization to a decision subject, with interests, influence and mode of engagement.
specific_questions: How does a stakeholder differ from a customer, an owner and a performer?
How is a conflict of interest recorded without treating a judgment of the person as a permanent property?
How is the map updated when the decision or the perimeter changes?
proposed_invariants: A role relates to a specific subject
Influence is an assessment with a method and a date
One subject may hold conflicting interests
EM-ORG-07.negative_case: A counterparty tagged "low influence" keeps that attribute forever across all projects.
EM-ORG-07.acceptance_scenario: Two projects yield different interest maps for the same counterparty; revising an assessment preserves the grounds and the history.
comparison_tracks: W3C ORG: collectives, roles, membership and posts
GLEIF: registered identity and consolidation relationships
Comparison of corporate governance, the actual org structure and the HR/ERP representation

EM-PEO-01.name: Person and Contextual Identity
EM-PEO-01.scope: The minimal identity of a natural person and permitted contacts. HR, customer and technical roles reference the person under a disclosure agreement.
specific_questions: How are namesakes distinguished, and how is merging people by email avoided?
When is a pseudonym or a local identifier sufficient?
How is a name change supported without losing history or over-disclosing?
proposed_invariants: Identity requires proof
Personal data is disclosed by purpose
An employer does not become the owner of all data about a person
EM-PEO-01.negative_case: Two users with the same display name are merged automatically.
EM-PEO-01.acceptance_scenario: Three systems, two namesakes and a name change yield correct bindings; an uncertain match remains a suggestion.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-02.name: Work Relationships and Assignments
EM-PEO-02.scope: Employment, contractor and agency relationships, the employee profile at the employer, assignments and entry/exit events. The onboarding process references process and access as links.
specific_questions: How are the employer, the labor customer and the staffing provider separated?
How are rehiring and several parallel relationships accounted for?
Which changes require a new relationship, and which a new version of an assignment?
proposed_invariants: An employee number is scoped to the employer
Changing the employer does not change the Person
Offboarding initiates an access review, it does not prove its completion
EM-PEO-02.negative_case: A freelancer is automatically recorded as a staff employee; closing the HR record is treated as revocation of all rights.
EM-PEO-02.acceptance_scenario: Show a secondary job, agency work, a return after termination, and an incomplete offboarding without loss of history.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-03.name: Competencies and Qualifications
EM-PEO-03.scope: Skill definition, proficiency scale, assessment, qualification credential and validity period. The professional role uses these definitions.
specific_questions: How do ESCO, SFIA and local scales relate?
How does a self-assessment differ from a verified credential?
How does comparability change when a scale is updated?
proposed_invariants: A skill definition is not possession of the skill
An assessment specifies the scale, method and date
Certificate expiry does not erase the fact of its issuance
EM-PEO-03.negative_case: A completed course automatically means expert level.
EM-PEO-03.acceptance_scenario: One competency is assessed by different methods and scales; the mapping shows the losses and does not invent an exact level translation.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-04.name: Recruitment and Hiring
EM-PEO-04.scope: The approved need, the vacancy, the candidacy, selection stages and the offer. Person, position, budget and the employment relationship have external owners.
specific_questions: How does a vacancy differ from a position and a candidacy?
How are one application for several openings, and one candidate for several vacancies, accounted for?
Which events terminate the retention and disclosure of candidate data?
proposed_invariants: A candidacy is bound to a vacancy and a period
An offer does not equal a started employment
A decision has an author, criteria and grounds
EM-PEO-04.negative_case: The presence of a CV is treated as consent to unlimited use across all group companies.
EM-PEO-04.acceptance_scenario: One application for two openings, three candidacies, a withdrawn offer and a rehire pass without duplicating the Person.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-05.name: Learning, Development and Succession
EM-PEO-05.scope: Training programs and participation, development plans, career paths and succession plans. The fact of training and a qualification are distinct.
specific_questions: What confirms a learning outcome beyond attendance?
How is a desired career separated from a managerial replacement plan?
How is disclosure of successor readiness assessments restricted?
proposed_invariants: A plan is not an HR decision
An outcome references a version of the learning objective
Succession does not automatically grant access to the position
EM-PEO-05.negative_case: The status "ready successor" is interpreted as an appointment to the post.
EM-PEO-05.acceptance_scenario: One course closes different development objectives; revising the succession plan does not change current assignments.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-06.name: Performance, Evidence and Calibration
EM-PEO-06.scope: The review cycle, criteria, observations, feedback, achievements, disputes and calibration decisions. Assessments must not become permanent properties of a person.
specific_questions: How are observation, contribution attribution, assessment and decision separated?
Which scales are comparable across roles and periods?
How are a negative event, the person's response and a revision stored without asserting fault?
proposed_invariants: An assessment is bound to a method and a period
Commit count is not identical to performance
A disputed claim does not become a confirmed fact by default
EM-PEO-06.negative_case: An automatic employee rating is built from closed tasks without regard to role, complexity and team contribution.
EM-PEO-06.acceptance_scenario: On one case, obtain different justified assessments, preserve an objection and a re-calibration; the public projection does not disclose individual assessments.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-07.name: Availability and Time Tracking
EM-PEO-07.scope: Work calendars, absence and available capacity; actual time records and their approval. Allocation of capacity across work items is a separate model.
specific_questions: How are planned availability, assigned load and actual time distinguished?
How are time zones, part-time schedules and overlapping records handled?
Which absence reasons does an operational consumer need?
proposed_invariants: Hours have a period and a time zone
The absence of a record does not equal zero
A medical reason is not included in the regular availability calendar
EM-PEO-07.negative_case: A worklog is used as proof of presence or of work quality.
EM-PEO-07.acceptance_scenario: A daylight saving transition, a half-time engagement, two projects and a timesheet correction do not produce negative or double capacity.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-08.name: Grades and Expectation Profiles
EM-PEO-08.scope: Versioned level systems, expectation profiles per role, level assignment and calibration. Level of responsibility, qualification and compensation are related but distinct.
specific_questions: How are job level, skill level and performance rating distinguished?
What evidence is sufficient to assign a grade?
How are migrations between local ladders handled in a company merger?
proposed_invariants: A grade specifies the scheme version
A level mapping may be partial
An assignment decision does not change the salary automatically
EM-PEO-08.negative_case: Middle in two companies is declared one global level without a crosswalk.
EM-PEO-08.acceptance_scenario: Map two ladders of different dimensionality, preserve incomparability and the revision history without overwriting assessments.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-PEO-09.name: Compensation and Benefits
EM-PEO-09.scope: Compensation ranges, individual assignments and benefit plans. Payroll calculation and mandatory rules are attached via jurisdictional profiles.
specific_questions: Which components have different periods and bases?
How is a position range separated from an individual contract?
How are aggregates published without reconstructing an individual's salary?
proposed_invariants: An amount has a currency and a period
A range is not an individual assignment
The fact of payment comes from a financial source
EM-PEO-09.negative_case: An average salary is disclosed for a group of one person, or via the difference of two reports.
EM-PEO-09.acceptance_scenario: Verify a partial engagement, several currencies, a mid-period change of terms and an unsafe aggregate over a small group.
comparison_tracks: HR Open: exchange of HR data
W3C ORG and ESCO/SFIA: relationships, skills and levels of responsibility
HRIS/ATS/LMS practice and independent verification of outcome measurement via SPACE

EM-STR-01.name: Strategy, Business Model and Value Streams
EM-STR-01.scope: Choice of markets, value proposition, the mechanism of producing outcomes, strategic hypotheses and the value stream. Projects do not substitute for strategy.
specific_questions: How are the mission, a strategic choice and an action plan distinguished?
How is a business model tested when the channel or segment changes?
What is a value stream stage, and what is an implementation process?
proposed_invariants: A hypothesis differs from a confirmed fact
A strategy has a horizon and a decision author
A value stream starts from the recipient's need
EM-STR-01.negative_case: A list of projects is called a strategy without a choice or an expected outcome.
EM-STR-01.acceptance_scenario: For a startup and a multi-industry group, link the choice, the value recipient, the assumptions and the revision criterion.
comparison_tracks: ArchiMate: motivation, capability and realization relationships
APQC: coverage of functions and processes
PMI: benefit/business case; compare with a chosen OKR school and value-stream management

EM-STR-02.name: Goals, Key Results and Benefits
EM-STR-02.scope: Goals, measurable target states, expected and realized benefits. The method of valuing benefit and harm is set by an explicit profile.
specific_questions: When does a deliverable actually produce an outcome?
How is a benefit linked to several work items without double counting?
How are value and negative consequences compared under incompatible scales?
proposed_invariants: A goal is not a metric
A target value specifies the metric version
Value/anti-value gets no universal formula without a methodology
EM-STR-02.negative_case: A planned effect is recorded as a realized result; a benefit is credited twice, to the program and to the project.
EM-STR-02.acceptance_scenario: One benefit from two projects, a delayed measurement and a negative side effect preserve attribution and uncertainty.
comparison_tracks: ArchiMate: motivation, capability and realization relationships
APQC: coverage of functions and processes
PMI: benefit/business case; compare with a chosen OKR school and value-stream management

EM-STR-03.name: Business Capabilities
EM-STR-03.scope: The enterprise's ability to achieve a defined class of outcomes independently of the current structure and means of implementation.
specific_questions: Where is the boundary of a capability relative to a process, a function and a product?
How are levels of detail formed without the org structure acting as the taxonomy?
Which methodology confirms maturity and coverage?
proposed_invariants: A capability survives reorganization
A maturity assessment is bound to a methodology
A system supports a capability, it does not automatically realize it in full
EM-STR-03.negative_case: A department name is used as the sole definition of a capability.
EM-STR-03.acceptance_scenario: After a process is transferred to another unit, the capability map keeps its IDs and changes only the realizations.
comparison_tracks: ArchiMate: motivation, capability and realization relationships
APQC: coverage of functions and processes
PMI: benefit/business case; compare with a chosen OKR school and value-stream management

EM-STR-04.name: Initiative and Investment Justification
EM-STR-04.scope: A proposed change, the problem, alternatives, the business case, assumptions and the decisions to move to execution.
specific_questions: When does a proposal become a project or operational work?
Which alternatives and uncertainties make the comparison honest?
How is the justification revised after the initial conditions change?
proposed_invariants: A business case is versioned
A rejected initiative keeps its grounds
Funding does not prove a realized benefit
EM-STR-04.negative_case: An initiative automatically becomes a project when a ticket is created.
EM-STR-04.acceptance_scenario: Compare two alternatives with a shared benefit, different risks and a changed forecast; the decision is reproducible as of a date.
comparison_tracks: ArchiMate: motivation, capability and realization relationships
APQC: coverage of functions and processes
PMI: benefit/business case; compare with a chosen OKR school and value-stream management

EM-WRK-01.name: Work Items and Delivery Flow
EM-WRK-01.scope: Tasks and typed work items, backlog, iterations, workflow, estimates and completion criteria. Jira types are adapters, not a universal ontology.
specific_questions: When is an Epic/Feature a work item, and when a product requirement?
How is meaning preserved across different source workflows?
Which statuses genuinely evidence an accepted result?
proposed_invariants: Done is defined by criteria and evidence
A tracker container is not a project
An effort estimate is not actual time
EM-WRK-01.negative_case: All Closed statuses automatically mean a completed and accepted result.
EM-WRK-01.acceptance_scenario: Move tasks between two workflows while keeping cancelled, rejected and accepted as distinct outcomes; a repeated import does not duplicate tasks.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-WRK-02.name: Project and Project Change Management
EM-WRK-02.scope: The business project, charter, plan, milestones, deliverables, acceptance and baseline changes. The product and the tracking system have separate identities.
specific_questions: How is a project's temporal boundary defined without mandating a waterfall methodology?
How do many-to-many relationships between projects, products and tracker containers work?
How are a forecast, an approved baseline and an actual result distinguished?
proposed_invariants: A project may have several tracker containers
A milestone is not a completed task
Closing a project does not close the product
EM-WRK-02.negative_case: One Jira Project is declared one business project for all the years of its existence.
EM-WRK-02.acceptance_scenario: Two projects share one tracker and one product; a change request changes the baseline while preserving the original commitment and the acceptance basis.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-WRK-03.name: Program and Benefits Management
EM-WRK-03.scope: Coordinated projects and other work pursued for joint benefits, with management of the transition and the sustainability of the effect.
specific_questions: What additional benefit justifies grouping the work?
How are non-project components and benefit completion after the projects accounted for?
How is the Program discriminator of the existing WM-ACT-029 applied?
proposed_invariants: Components are not limited to projects
The program owner does not own all facts of the projects
The joint effect has an explicit justification
EM-WRK-03.negative_case: An arbitrary folder of unrelated projects is called a program.
EM-WRK-03.acceptance_scenario: Model a program with two projects and an operational transition; a closed project does not mean the joint benefit has been achieved.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-WRK-04.name: Portfolio and Investment Selection
EM-WRK-04.scope: Selection and balancing of initiatives, projects, programs and product investments within the strategy and its constraints.
specific_questions: How does a portfolio differ from a program and a catalog?
How are alternatives and limited resources handled without double funding?
How are projects and continuous product investments compared?
proposed_invariants: The composition has a basis and a period
Components may be independent of each other
A rank is not an objective property of the work
EM-WRK-04.negative_case: All portfolio elements are automatically required to form one program.
EM-WRK-04.acceptance_scenario: Two portfolios use one initiative with different funding shares; the chosen scenario preserves the decision criteria.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-WRK-05.name: Capacity and Resource Allocation
EM-WRK-05.scope: Demand, available capacity and assignments of human and other resources to work. Human engagement, money and compute have different units.
specific_questions: How are a competency demand and available capacity matched?
How are shared teams and indivisible resources accounted for?
When is exceeding 100% an error, and when different scenarios?
proposed_invariants: Units and a calendar are mandatory
A plan does not substitute for the actuals
A conflict is checked within one scenario and interval
EM-WRK-05.negative_case: FTE, GPU hours and a money budget are summed into one capacity.
EM-WRK-05.acceptance_scenario: Two projects compete for one specialist and a GPU pool; the plan surfaces the overlap without changing the employment terms.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-WRK-06.name: Dependencies and Impact Analysis
EM-WRK-06.scope: Typed cross-object dependencies, prerequisites and constraints with scope and evidence. Does not imply automatic causality.
specific_questions: Which edges permit transitivity?
How are blocking, usage, funding and a causal claim distinguished?
How is graph incompleteness accounted for in impact analysis?
proposed_invariants: Type and direction are mandatory
A cycle is allowed only under the rules of the specific type
The absence of an edge does not prove independence
EM-WRK-06.negative_case: Any path in the graph is declared a proven causal chain.
EM-WRK-06.acceptance_scenario: For an API change and a resource delay, obtain different impact sets; unknown relationships reduce the completeness of the answer.
comparison_tracks: PMI: project/program/portfolio
Process-based and flow-based organization of work; compare Scrum/Kanban against primary sources
Tracker object practice: container, issue, workflow and binding to the business initiative

EM-PRD-01.name: Product, Offering and Roadmap
EM-PRD-01.scope: The product as a managed outcome for a consumer, offering variants, prices and development intents. The physical instance, the software and the actual delivery have separate boundaries.
specific_questions: When does an edition continue a product, and when does it form a new one?
How is a roadmap promise separated from a contractual obligation?
How are a free, an internal and a physical product described on one foundation?
proposed_invariants: An offering has a market and a period
A price has a currency and a unit
A roadmap item does not prove the existence of a feature
EM-PRD-01.negative_case: A single pricing change creates a new software product.
EM-PRD-01.acceptance_scenario: Map SaaS, a device and an internal product: the shared meaning is preserved, and the profile does not impose a subscription on the device.

EM-PRD-02.name: Service and Service Model
EM-PRD-02.scope: The service, the expected outcome, the terms of provision and consumption. The running service instance and the service level agreement are delegated.
specific_questions: How does a service differ from a product and a process?
Can an internal service have no price?
How is one service linked to several providers and implementations?
proposed_invariants: The consumer is not the technical API client
A service does not contain a copy of the runtime
The expected outcome is separated from the measured one
EM-PRD-02.negative_case: An API endpoint is automatically declared a business service.
EM-PRD-02.acceptance_scenario: Describe an HR service and a digital platform service with different implementations and a shared way of specifying the outcome.
comparison_tracks: TM Forum SID: product/service/resource and commercial roles
IDTA AAS: physical assets and composite descriptions
Product management and engineering configuration; compare selected PLM and software practices

EM-PRD-03.name: Requirements and expected behavior
EM-PRD-03.scope: Requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria and traceability to the solution. An implementation task references a requirement.
specific_questions: How to distinguish a need, a requirement, a feature and a task?
What changes when a new baseline is set?
How to represent a conflict between requirements of different stakeholders?
proposed_invariants: The requirement version is pinned at acceptance
A closed task does not prove fulfillment
A conflict does not erase the alternative
EM-PRD-03.negative_case: Moving a ticket to Done automatically confirms all linked requirements.
EM-PRD-03.acceptance_scenario: Verify one requirement with three tasks and a failed test, then the compatibility of two baselines.
comparison_tracks: TM Forum SID: product/service/resource and commercial roles
IDTA AAS: physical assets and composite descriptions
Product management and engineering configuration; compare selected PLM and software practices

EM-PRD-04.name: Research, hypothesis and experiment
EM-PRD-04.scope: Research question, hypothesis, experiment design, run and interpretation of the result. AI training and evaluation use specialized child models.
specific_questions: Which conditions make a result reproducible?
How to distinguish absence of effect from absence of data?
How to link a negative result to a subsequent decision?
proposed_invariants: The hypothesis precedes result evaluation or is marked post-hoc
A run pins the versions of its inputs
A conclusion states its limits of applicability
EM-PRD-04.negative_case: A failed experiment is deleted and the hypothesis is replaced retroactively.
EM-PRD-04.acceptance_scenario: Two runs of one design with different inputs and contradictory results remain distinguishable and reproducible.
comparison_tracks: TM Forum SID: product/service/resource and commercial roles
IDTA AAS: physical assets and composite descriptions
Product management and engineering configuration; compare selected PLM and software practices

EM-PRD-05.name: Intellectual property and usage rights
EM-PRD-05.scope: Protected object, application, registration, ownership and licensed use. The brand as a business association is separated from the trademark.
specific_questions: How does a patent application differ from a granted right?
How to model territory and term?
How to separate the creator, the owner and the licensee?
proposed_invariants: A right has a subject and a basis
Registration is not universal across all countries
A license does not transfer ownership without a basis
EM-PRD-05.negative_case: A company logo automatically proves an exclusive right worldwide.
EM-PRD-05.acceptance_scenario: Show one brand with two territorial registrations and a license expiring earlier than the registration.
comparison_tracks: TM Forum SID: product/service/resource and commercial roles
IDTA AAS: physical assets and composite descriptions
Product management and engineering configuration; compare selected PLM and software practices

EM-COM-01.name: Relationships with customers, suppliers and partners
EM-COM-01.scope: Counterparty roles, relationships, contact assignments and segmentation. The person or organization itself is reused by identity.
specific_questions: How does one organization become both a customer and a supplier?
What does a customer account mean for a group of legal entities?
Where is the boundary between B2B and B2C profiles?
proposed_invariants: A counterparty role does not create a new Party
A contact has a term and a context
A segment is a classification with a source
EM-COM-01.negative_case: An organization is duplicated after the first purchase from an existing customer.
EM-COM-01.acceptance_scenario: One Party with three commercial roles, different contacts and two contracts does not produce three identities.

EM-COM-02.name: Sales and marketing interactions
EM-COM-02.scope: Lead, opportunity, quote, campaign and attribution. Counterparty relationships and concluded contracts have their own owners.

How does a contractual SLA differ from an internal SLO?
How to record a dispute over performance?

An amendment does not overwrite the signed text
An obligation has a debtor, a subject and a criterion of performance
